reforms.description: The Federal Government has rapidly expanded manpower training and mobility programmes, significantly increasing expenditures to improve the skills and adaptability of the labor force, particularly in regions with low educational standards. Additionally, a Federal Winter Job Expansion Plan was announced to combat seasonal unemployment, aiming to create over 140,000 jobs through various direct job-creation projects.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving skills and creating jobs enhances labor productivity and adaptability, contributing positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been put into action as indicated by their implementation status.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms significantly enhance workforce skills and job creation but do not represent a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: In the 1970-1971 fiscal year, about C$ 297 million was spent on Federal manpower training and mobility programmes, compared to about C$ 108 million only three years earlier.

reforms.description: The 8th May 1972 Federal budget introduced measures for faster write-off of machinery and equipment costs in manufacturing, alongside a reduction in corporate tax rates for manufacturing and processing profits.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These tax incentives are designed to stimulate investment in manufacturing, thereby enhancing productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The measures have been enacted as part of the Federal budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of significant tax measures represents a major reform in the innovation support system for manufacturing.
reforms.source_quote: New measures proposed in the 8th May Federal budget include faster write-off of the costs of machinery and equipment used for the purpose of manufacturing or processing.
